text:
Jacob Markstrom made the difference in Columbus. The Panthers goalie, a second-round pick of Florida's in 2008 out of Brynas in Sweden, stopped 37 of 38 shots, and by our numbers he saved about two goals more than the quality of those chances called for. His best moment came in the third period, when he turned away a 22 percent look from Matthew Knies. FLA beat CBJ 4-1, the second win over Columbus this season after a 7-3 result on Oct. 13.

The score hides how lopsided the game was. Columbus took 73 shot attempts to Florida's 48 and won 35 of 57 faceoffs. Our deserved-to-win number, the share of simulated replays of every shot in which a team comes out ahead, gave CBJ 56 percent. The Blue Jackets also outplayed Florida in the third, 1.32 expected goals to 0.39 (expected goals measure the quality of chances), yet allowed two goals there. Sam Bennett's wrist shot at 14:29, a 6 percent chance, made it 3-1, and Sam Reinhart's backhand at 17:44 sealed it.

Bennett scored twice, and the first came on Florida's only power play, a snap shot two minutes into the second period. Lars Eller added a goal 2:17 later, and Ivan Provorov cut the lead to 2-1 late in the period. Columbus then spent the rest of the night chasing a goalie who wouldn't give way. The data we have doesn't show where this leaves either team's streak or record, but it does show the Blue Jackets did most things right and still lost.
